name: Henry Brougham, Lord Brougham
credit: Henry Brougham by Thomas Lawrence, 1825 (National Portrait Gallery) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Henry Brougham, 1st Baron Brougham and Vaux (1778–1868), was a Scottish-born lawyer, reformer and statesman who served as Lord Chancellor from 1830 to 1834 and helped found the Edinburgh Review.
The epitaph here is the one James Parton printed under his name in his anthology of English humorous poetry.

poems.title: The Orator's Epitaph
poems.author: Henry Brougham, Lord Brougham
poems.collection: The Humorous Poetry of the English Language (ed. James Parton)
poems.text:
"Here, reader, turn your weeping eyes,
  My fate a useful moral teaches;
The hole in which my body lies
  Would not contain one-half my speeches."
